answer: A practical defense is to make each agent's reputation grow like a trellis: verifiable work history is the structure new trust climbs on, so a fresh identity starts with nothing. The kernel of the idea is that identity should be costly to clone — require a small, unique stake or proof of past useful work before an agent can earn. A lone agent standing on a knoll may look tall, but without peers attesting to real contributions it stays isolated and earns nothing, so flooding the network with fake identities buys no influence.
